mutation.m1.person.jan1_2001_2002: Mutation fixture (the January 1 birthday question of the years 2001 and 2002), inputs of mutation.eic.mfj_no_child_20000 with the years of birth changed: the taxpayer born on January 1, 2001, the spouse on January 1, 2002 (each asked 'Were you born on January 1?' because the year is one in which that date decides an age test); expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator. A person reaches an age on the day before the birthday (i1040gi p. 110, Schedule 1-A, 'A person is considered to reach age 65 on the day before the person’s 65th birthday'; i8615 p. 1, Certain January 1 birthdays). Taxpayer: i1040gi p. 41, EIC Step 4, question 2, 'were born after December 31, 1960, and before January 2, 2001': a January 1, 2001 birth is before January 2, 2001, so the age-25 test is met (person.eic_age25 true). Spouse: i8615 p. 1 chart, a child born on 'January 1, 2002' is considered to be 24 at the end of 2025, so not under 24 (person.under24 false); for i8863 p. 7, Line 7, question 1, 'Were you under age 24 at the end of 2025?', the answer is No, so the spouse is 24 or older (person.edu_age24 true).
mutation.m1.person.born_2002_not_jan1_an: Mutation fixture (a 2002 birth that is not on January 1, and a January 1, 2007 birth), inputs of mutation.eic.mfj_no_child_20000 with the years of birth changed: the taxpayer born in 2002, not on January 1; the spouse born on January 1, 2007; expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator. Taxpayer: born after January 1, 2002, so 23 at the end of 2025 (i8615 p. 1, Certain January 1 birthdays; i8863 p. 7, Line 7, question 1): under 24 (person.under24 true) and not 24 or older (person.edu_age24 false). Spouse: born on January 1, 2007, reaches 19 on December 31, 2025 (a person reaches an age on the day before the birthday), so older than 18 for i8863 p. 7, Line 7, 'b. Age 18 at the end of 2025' (person.edu_over18 true), and born after January 1, 2002, so under 24 (person.under24 true).
mutation.m1.person.jan1_2008: Mutation fixture (a January 1, 2008 birth for the saver's credit age test, and the HSA prior-excess question of a person with no HSA), inputs of mutation.eic.line5_key.no_child with the year of birth 2008 and 'Were you born on January 1?' Yes, and with no answer to the earlier-year excess HSA contributions question, which is asked only of a person who listed a health savings account; expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator. f8880 p. 2, Who Can Take This Credit: the person who made the contribution must not have been 'born after January 1, 2008'; a person born on January 1, 2008 was not, so the age condition is met (person.sav_born true: born before January 2, 2008). The person listed no Form 8889, so the earlier-year excess HSA question does not apply and its gate is No (person.x_hsa_prior_excess_if_hsa false).
mutation.m1.person.born_2010_under16: Mutation fixture (a person born in 2010 who states being under 16 at the end of 2025), inputs of mutation.eic.line5_key.no_child with the year of birth 2010 and 'Were you under age 16 at the end of 2025?' Yes; expected value predicted by hand before running the evaluator: i1040gi p. 66, Self-Select PIN, 'a first-time filer under age 16 at the end of 2025'; a person born in 2010 is 15 or 16 at the end of 2025 depending on the birth date, which the year alone leaves open, so the stated answer decides: under 16 (person.under16 true).
mutation.m1.person.born_2010_not_under16: Mutation fixture (a person born in 2010 who states not being under 16 at the end of 2025), inputs of mutation.eic.line5_key.no_child with the year of birth 2010 and 'Were you under age 16 at the end of 2025?' No; expected value predicted by hand before running the evaluator: i1040gi p. 66, Self-Select PIN, 'a first-time filer under age 16 at the end of 2025'; the year 2010 leaves the age open, and the stated answer decides: not under 16 (person.under16 false).
mutation.m1.person.born_1976_age50_both_: Mutation fixture (two people born in 1976, one 50 at the end of 2025 and one not), inputs of mutation.eic.mfj_no_child_20000 with both years of birth 1976, the taxpayer answering Yes and the spouse No to 'Were you 50 or older at the end of 2025?'; expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator. i1040gi p. 97, IRA Deduction Worksheet, '$8,000 if age 50 or older at the end of 2025': the taxpayer is (person.ira_age50 true), the spouse is not (person.ira_age50 false). p560 chapter 3, Catch-up contributions, 'age 50 or over at the end of the calendar year' and the 60-to-63 band 'in a tax year in which they attain age 60, 61, 62, or 63': the taxpayer's SIMPLE catch-up band is 50 or over (person.simple_age age50), the spouse's is under 50 (under50).
mutation.m1.person.born_1971_age55_and_1: Mutation fixture (a person born in 1971 who states being 55 at the end of 2025, and a person born in 1970), inputs of mutation.eic.mfj_no_child_20000 with the taxpayer born in 1971 answering Yes to 'Were you age 55 or older at the end of 2025?' and the spouse born in 1970; expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator. i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 6, 'If, at the end of 2025, you were age 55 or older': for a person born in 1971 the year leaves this open and the stated answer decides (person.age55_at_year_end_if_open_year true). The spouse, born in 1970, is 55 at the end of 2025, within 50 to 59 for the SIMPLE catch-up (p560 chapter 3, 'age 50 or over at the end of the calendar year', the higher band only for those who attain 60 to 63 in the year): person.simple_age age50. i5329 p. 8, Lines 52a and 52b, 'following the year in which you reach age 73': the taxpayer, born in 1971, is 54, so not of that age (person.rmd_age false).
mutation.m1.person.simple_open_years: Mutation fixture (the SIMPLE catch-up band of people born in 1962 and 1966, as they state it), inputs of mutation.eic.mfj_no_child_20000 with the taxpayer born in 1962 stating the band 50 or over (64 at the end of 2025) and the spouse born in 1966 stating the band 60 to 63 (60 at the end of 2025); expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator. p560 chapter 3, Catch-up contributions, the higher limit applies 'in a tax year in which they attain age 60, 61, 62, or 63': a person born in 1962 attains 63 or 64 in 2025 and one born in 1966 attains 59 or 60, so the year leaves the band open and the stated answer decides: taxpayer age50 (64, past the band), spouse age60_63 (person.simple_age).
mutation.m1.person.died_at_64_and_born_1: Mutation fixture (a person born in 1960 whose final return this is, having died in 2025 before reaching 65, and a person born in 1961 not on January 1), inputs of mutation.eic.mfj_no_child_20000 with the taxpayer born in 1960 answering Yes to 'Is this the final return of a person who died in 2025 before reaching age 65?' and the spouse born in 1961 answering No to 'Were you born on January 1?'; both have an SSN; expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator. i1040gi p. 110, Schedule 1-A, Part V, Death of a taxpayer in 2025, 'If a taxpayer was born before January 2, 1961, but died in 2025 before reaching age 65 ...': the taxpayer is such a person (person.died_before_65 true); the taxpayer has an SSN (person.tin_or_itin_applied true; i1040gi p. 17). The spouse, born in 1961 after January 1, reaches 65 in 2026, so 2025 is not the year of reaching 65 (person.turned_65_this_year false).
mutation.m1.person.rmd_age_and_inherited: Mutation fixture (the possibility of a required minimum distribution: by age, and by an inherited account), inputs of mutation.eic.mfj_no_child_20000 with the taxpayer born in 1950 (not asked about an inherited account) and the spouse, born in 1980, answering Yes to the inherited IRA or plan account question; neither missed a required distribution; expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator. i5329 p. 8, Lines 52a and 52b, a required minimum distribution is due for the year 'following the year in which you reach age 73', and a beneficiary of an inherited account can owe one at any age: the taxpayer (75 at the end of 2025) can owe one (person.rmd_possible true); the spouse inherited an account (person.inherited_account_if_under_73 true), so can owe one (person.rmd_possible true).
mutation.m1.person.hsa_prior_excess_born: Mutation fixture (an HSA holder born in 1950 with earlier-year excess HSA contributions), inputs of mutation.t2.f8889.dec_none_changed_all_year with the year of birth 1950 (not asked about an inherited account) and Yes to the question of earlier-year excess HSA contributions not removed before 2025; expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator. The person listed a Form 8889 (person.has_hsa true), and so is asked the earlier-year excess question, answered Yes (person.x_hsa_prior_excess_if_hsa true; i5329 Part VII, Additional Tax on Excess Contributions to Health Savings Accounts, which this tool does not prepare). Born in 1950, the person is of the age at which a required distribution is due (i5329 p. 8, Lines 52a and 52b, 'following the year in which you reach age 73'), so the inherited-account question is not asked and its gate is No (person.inherited_account_if_under_73 false).
mutation.m1.person.birth_year_after_tax_: Mutation fixture (a year of birth after the tax year), inputs of mutation.eic.line5_key.no_child with the year of birth 2026; expected values predicted by hand before running the evaluator: a person on a 2025 return cannot have been born after 2025 (the consistency bound of the parameter age.birth_year_latest, cited to i1040gi p. 33, Line 12d), so the year is flagged as not possible (person.birth_year_bad true) and the household count of such people is above zero (household.birth_year_bad true).
